ns1:item.ns1:title: Coding and decoding urban nature
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00521-0

Urban nature — from street trees and parks to soils, waterways and the organisms they support — is crucial to sustainable and livable cities. In this Focus issue, we showcase how these living systems are increasingly coded through digital technologies, and how new forms of knowledge are emerging to decode complex ecological processes and guide urban environmental management.
ns1:item.dc:title: Coding and decoding urban nature

ns1:item.ns1:title: Guests in the city
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00484-2

In Singapore, a seat offered on the train and workers carried at the back of lorries changed how Ziheng Zeng understood both his own temporary place in the city and the different ways an orderly city carries those it asks to stay.
ns1:item.dc:title: Guests in the city
ns1:item.dc:creator: Ziheng Zeng

ns1:item.ns1:title: Urbanization promotes biological invasions in global cities
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Cities, Published online: 16 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s44284-026-00517-w

Urbanization significantly influences biological invasions, with developed cities exhibiting higher non-native vertebrate richness. Key factors include propagule pressure, habitat modification and climate, emphasizing the need for targeted management strategies to mitigate invasions and enhance urban sustainability.
